scope: Transformer autoregressive inference; KV Cache sizing example is explicitly illustrative and uses the stated Llama 3 8B structure assumptions.

claims.claim: Autoregressive generation predicts a next token conditioned on previously available tokens.
claims.notes: Tokenization units are model-tokenizer dependent; token is not synonymous with a word or Chinese character.

claims.claim: Prefill processes prompt tokens and Decode advances generation using cached key/value states.
claims.notes: Compute- versus memory-bound behavior depends on sequence length, batch size, hardware, backend and configuration.

claims.claim: For standard attention KV storage, bytes scale with 2 × layers × KV heads × head dimension × cached tokens × bytes per element.
claims.notes: The chapter's 128 KiB/token and 1 GiB/8192-token figures are arithmetic derived from 32 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128 and FP16. Excludes runtime overhead and deployment-specific sharding.

claims.claim: TTFT, ITL/TPOT, end-to-end latency and throughput describe different aspects of inference service quality.
claims.notes: Definitions and aggregation windows should be checked against the selected benchmark tool.

claims.claim: In ordinary autoregressive generation, logits at the final prompt position predict the first generated token; subsequent decode steps consume sampled tokens.
claims.locator: Prompt logprob code: last prompt row predicts first decode token
claims.notes: The SVG presents the logical single-request, non-disaggregated path. Chunked prefill, P/D disaggregation and speculative decoding can change the physical execution steps.
